data.narrative:
Neros, a Series C defense and security company founded by Soren Monroe-Anderson and Olaf Hichwa, is valued at $2.5B post-money following $250M in cumulative fundraising. The peer universe comprises 12 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables: 2 public companies (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 10 private firms including Quantum-Systems ($8.0B Series C), Helsing ($18.0B Series D), Saronic ($9.2B Series D), and Chaos Industries ($4.5B Series D).

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression modeling uses the $2.5B last post-money as a base and applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical for Series C advancement, implying $4.2B. Peer-median benchmarking across the 12-company cohort yields a median valuation of $1.8B, with a range spanning $300M to $18.0B. The wide peer range reflects heterogeneity in technology maturity and market traction within the sector.

Triangulating both methods produces a valuation range of $1.5B (low) to $4.9B (high), with a median of $3.0B. The current $2.5B valuation sits in the lower-middle portion of this range. Key uncertainties include the degree of comparability across peer-stage heterogeneity (the peer set spans Series B through Series D) and the applicability of historical step-up multiples in the current defense tech funding environment.
